title: Fix the maintenance step
prompt: Rewrite this instruction so a tired mechanic at 3 a.m. gets it right the first time. Active voice. Short sentences. Simple words.
source: Prior to the commencement of the removal procedure, it should be ensured that electrical power has been disconnected from the unit by the technician in order to prevent injury.
intent: Tell the reader to disconnect electrical power from the unit before they start to remove it, because it can cause injury. One clear command in the imperative. It must not lose the order (disconnect first, then remove) or the reason (injury).
hints: Put the reason in its own short sentence, or as a WARNING before the step.
exampleGood: WARNING: Electrical power can cause injury. Disconnect the power from the unit before you remove it.

title: One step, one action
prompt: Rewrite this as clear numbered steps or short sentences. Keep every action. Keep the order.
source: Utilize the provided key to unlock the panel, subsequently removing the cover and performing a visual inspection of the filter, which should be replaced if a sufficient amount of dirt is observed.
intent: Steps in order: unlock the panel with the key; remove the cover; look at (inspect) the filter; replace the filter if it is dirty. A great answer also makes 'dirty' testable (e.g. 'if you cannot see light through it').
hints: "Sufficient amount of dirt" is vague. What can the mechanic actually see?
exampleGood:
1. Unlock the panel with the key.
2. Remove the cover.
3. Look at the filter.
4. If you cannot see light through the filter, replace it.

title: Explain a password
prompt: Explain what a password is and why it matters, using only simple, everyday words. Two sentences max.
intent: A password is a secret word or set of letters that only you know; you type it to show the computer or site that it is really you, so other people cannot get into your things.
hints: Who knows it? What does typing it prove?
Words like "authenticate" and "credential" are not allowed. Say what they mean.
exampleGood: A password is a secret word that only you know. You type it so the computer knows it is really you and not someone else.

title: Explain a backup
prompt: Explain what a backup is to someone who has never used a computer. Simple, everyday words only.
intent: A backup is a second copy of your files kept in another place, so that if the first copy is lost or broken you can get your things back.
hints: Think of a photo you print twice and keep in two houses.
exampleGood: A backup is a second copy of your work that you keep in another place. If your computer breaks or is lost, you can get your work back from the copy.

title: Bottom line up front
prompt: Your boss has 10 seconds. Write the first line of your reply to this thread. 15 words max. Lead with the decision you need.
source: Hi all, following up on last week's sync. The vendor got back to us and the new pricing is 18% higher than budgeted. We have two options: accept and cut the Q3 contractor spend, or delay the rollout to Q4 and renegotiate. Finance says either works but they need an answer by Friday, otherwise the old contract auto-renews at the higher rate anyway. Engineering prefers the delay. Thoughts?
intent: Ask the boss to decide by Friday between (a) accepting the 18% higher vendor price and cutting Q3 contractor spend, or (b) delaying the rollout to Q4 to renegotiate. A great answer gives a recommendation and the Friday deadline.
hints: What do you need from the reader, and by when?
Details can come after the first line.
exampleGood: Decision by Friday: I recommend delaying rollout to Q4 to renegotiate the 18% price rise.

title: Make it testable
prompt: Rewrite this support promise so a customer and a manager would both agree whether it was kept.
source: We will try to respond to urgent tickets quickly, usually within a reasonable time, and keep customers informed as needed.
intent: A measurable promise: a defined class of urgent tickets gets a first human response within a fixed time (e.g. 1 hour), during defined hours, and the customer gets updates on a fixed schedule (e.g. every 4 hours) until resolved.
hints: Replace each vague word with a number.
Define "urgent" in a way anyone can check.
exampleGood: We send a first human reply to every P1 ticket (site down or data loss) within 1 hour, 24/7. Until it is fixed, we post an update every 4 hours.

title: Who is "it"?
prompt: This sentence can be read two ways. Rewrite it so only one reading is possible. Assume the virus scanner checks the uploaded file.
source: When the user uploads the file to the server, it is scanned and, if it fails, it is deleted.
intent: The uploaded file is scanned for viruses; if the file fails the scan, the file (not the server, not the user) is deleted.
hints: Replace every "it" with the noun you mean.
exampleGood: When a user uploads a file, the server scans the file for viruses. If the file fails the scan, the server deletes the file.

title: And, or, or both?
prompt: The discount should apply to students, to seniors, and to people who are both. Rewrite the rule so nobody can argue about it.
source: A 10% discount applies to students and/or seniors.
intent: Anyone who is a student, a senior, or both gets exactly one 10% discount (discounts do not stack for people who are both).
hints: Does a student who is also a senior get 10% or 20%? Say it.
exampleGood: Customers who are students, seniors, or both get one 10% discount. The discount does not stack.

title: The auto-lock door
prompt: Write one EARS requirement: the door should lock itself when nobody has opened it for a while. Use the template "When <trigger>, the <system> shall <response>."
intent: When the door has been closed for a fixed time (a specific number of seconds) with no one opening it, the door controller shall lock the door. The time must be a number.
placeholder: When the door ..., the door controller shall ...
hints: "For a while" is vague. Pick a number.
What starts the timer: the door closing?
exampleGood: When the door has been closed for 30 seconds, the door controller shall lock the door.

title: Low battery warning
prompt: Write an EARS requirement for this: if the battery gets low while the drone is flying, it should come home. Use "While ..., when ..., the ... shall ..." or "If ..., then the ... shall ...".
intent: While the drone is in flight, when the battery charge falls below a fixed percentage, the drone shall return to its launch point. 'Low' must be a number.
placeholder: While the drone is flying, when ...
hints: "Home" could mean the owner's house. Name the place.
exampleGood: While the drone is in flight, when the battery charge falls below 20%, the drone shall return to the launch point.
